record.vts_boundary_basis: 33 CFR 167.1312 places the southern lanes at about 48°09.4'N to 48°12.9'N, 123°23.8'W to 123°32.9'W (off Port Angeles), east of 124°40'W and south of the Church Point-Race Rocks-48°17.88'N 123°14.1'W line. That falls wholly within the CVTS area (33 CFR 161.55(a)) and within the Seattle Traffic Ch 5A service area (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10)(ii); RAMN 2026 s.3.5.4.2, which covers Canadian and US waters there). The lanes lie south of the western-lanes separation zone and, on the points checked, south of the international boundary, i.e. in the VTS Puget Sound legal area; the boundary line itself was not plotted.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (project list VRS-0001 to VRS-0023 has none on the North American Pacific coast). Reporting under 33 CFR 161 subpart B (VMRS sailing plan, position and final reports) and Canadian SOR/2025-275 sailing plan/position reports is the participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the VTS, not as a separate MRS.
record.evidence_summary: Individual TSS inside the CVTS area and the Seattle Traffic Ch 5A sector by statute (33 CFR 161.55, 161.12) and by CCG RAMN 2026. VTS PS manual says the IMO TSS is in the VTSPS area and radar covers all waters where the TSS exists. No IMO or separate national MRS.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS only confirmed at individual-TSS level, but the Seattle Traffic Ch 5A sector serves these lanes, not Victoria Traffic; the Prince Rupert/approaches points in the lead relate to other TSS

record.vts_sector: Seattle Traffic Ch 5A (Rosario Strait, approaches, Admiralty Inlet north of Nodule Point-Bush Point); Seattle Traffic Ch 14 (Puget Sound south of Nodule Point-Bush Point)
record.vts_boundary_basis: The scheme (33 CFR 167.1320-1323: Rosario Strait, approaches to Puget Sound other than Rosario Strait, and Puget Sound) lies entirely in US waters of the Salish Sea, which is the VTS Puget Sound area under 33 CFR 161.55. Table 1 to 161.12(c) item (10)(i)-(ii) assigns these waters to Seattle Traffic Ch 14 and Ch 5A. The northern end of the Rosario Strait part (about 48°49'N 122°55'W) reaches the Patos Island-Alden Bank line, beyond which Victoria Traffic serves. The parts north-west of the McCurdy Point-Point Partridge line are also in the CVTS area. VTS PS manual: the IMO TSS is in the VTSPS area and radar covers all waters where the TSS exists.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (project list VRS-0001 to VRS-0023 has none on the North American Pacific coast). Reporting under 33 CFR 161 subpart B (VMRS sailing plan, position and final reports) and Canadian SOR/2025-275 sailing plan/position reports is the participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the VTS, not as a separate MRS. Canadian SOR/2025-275 is not relevant (no Canadian waters).
record.evidence_summary: Entire TSS in US waters within the statutory VTS Puget Sound area; the operator's 2024 user manual names the IMO TSS as in the VTSPS area. The VTS Special Area (Eastern San Juan Island Archipelago, 33 CFR 161.55(b)) covers Rosario Strait. No IMO or separate national MRS.
record.source_date: 33 CFR 161/167 eCFR 2026-09-01; VTS PS User's Manual 2024

record.vts_sector: Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1, Victoria Traffic Ch 11 (CVTS service area for Haro Strait and Boundary Pass on both sides of the boundary)
record.vts_boundary_basis: The TSS (33 CFR 167.1331; COLREG.2/Circ.51 Part I) runs from precautionary area V off Victoria through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass, along the international boundary. Canadian waters: the Victoria VTS Zone limit follows the boundary through Boundary Pass and Haro Strait (SOR/2025-275 Sch.1 item 1; RAMN Table 3-1 Sector 1). US waters: VTS Puget Sound area to the boundary (33 CFR 161.55) and inside the CVTS. Under the CVTS, Victoria Traffic Ch 11 serves all Canadian and US waters of Haro Strait and Boundary Pass north and west of the Church Point-Race Rocks-Hein Bank-Cattle Point exchange line (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10)(iv); RAMN s.3.5.4.3).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (project list VRS-0001 to VRS-0023 has none on the North American Pacific coast). Reporting under 33 CFR 161 subpart B (VMRS sailing plan, position and final reports) and Canadian SOR/2025-275 sailing plan/position reports is the participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the VTS, not as a separate MRS.
record.evidence_summary: Statutory Canadian Victoria VTS Zone and US VTS Puget Sound areas meet at the boundary along the TSS; the CVTS service is delivered by Victoria Traffic for the whole Haro Strait/Boundary Pass segment (RAMN 2026 s.3.5.4.3 names Haro Strait and Boundary Passage). No IMO or separate national MRS.
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only (Victoria VTS Zone plus VTS Puget Sound); the 'Vancouver' centre in 33 CFR 161.55(a) is outdated, since RAMN 2026 names MCTS Victoria (Patricia Bay)

record.vts_boundary_basis: The TSS (COLREG.2/Circ.51 Part II; 33 CFR 167.1332) runs from precautionary area GS (about 48°48'N to 48°55'N, 122°54'W to 123°07'W) through PR to the lane ends at about 49°04.5'N 123°20'W, crossing the boundary. Canadian waters, including the part north of 49°N, are in Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 (SOR/2025-275 Sch.1 item 1; RAMN Table 3-1, whose Sector 1 line runs from 49°00'N 123°05'20"W to Roberts Bank and Sandheads, leaving the TSS inside). US waters are in the VTS Puget Sound legal area (33 CFR 161.55) and the CVTS (north limit 49°N). The service provider for Boundary Pass and the southern Strait of Georgia on both sides of the boundary is Victoria Traffic Ch 11, north-west of the Patos Island-Alden Bank line (33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 item (10)(iv); RAMN s.3.5.4.3).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (project list VRS-0001 to VRS-0023 has none on the North American Pacific coast). Reporting under 33 CFR 161 subpart B (VMRS sailing plan, position and final reports) and Canadian SOR/2025-275 sailing plan/position reports is the participation duty of the VTS and is recorded with the VTS, not as a separate MRS.
record.evidence_summary: Canadian statutory Victoria VTS Zone Sector 1 covers the Canadian part (including north of 49°N, outside the CVTS). US waters are in the VTS Puget Sound area; the CVTS service is delivered by Victoria Traffic. No IMO or separate national MRS.
record.prior_lead_outcome: confirmed: VTS only; the part north of 49°N is Canadian-only (Victoria VTS Zone), as in the lead

record.vts_centre: Vessel Traffic Center, Yerba Buena Island (San Francisco Traffic)
record.vts_sector: Offshore Sector (San Francisco Traffic Ch 12; Offshore Precautionary Area Ch 14)
record.vts_boundary_basis: The VTS area includes seaward approaches within 38 nm of Mount Tamalpais (33 CFR 161.50). The VTS SF User Manual (Apr 2025) defines the Offshore Sector the same way, names the San Francisco Offshore TSS (Northern, Western and Southern lanes and Main Ship Channel) and sets Offshore Sector reporting procedures for it (MSIB 13-04). On the current IMO coordinates (COLREG.2/Circ.64, in force 1 June 2013) the Western approach (<=32.5 nm), Southern approach (<=37.7 nm), Main Ship Channel and Precautionary Area are inside 38 nm. The outer end of the Northern approach (about 38°06.9'N-38°10.1'N, 123°20.3'W-123°21.8'W) lies about 38.8 nm away, i.e. roughly 0.8 nm beyond the arc (computed). Coverage is therefore partial but nearly complete. eCFR 167.402-404 still show the pre-2013 coordinates (all within ~30 nm).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system on this coast (W-S18). VMRS reports to VTS San Francisco (33 CFR 161 subpart B; Offshore Sector sailing plan 15 minutes before the VTS boundary) are VTS participation duties, not a separate MRS.
record.voluntary_reporting: Yes: Offshore Vessel Movement Reporting System (OVMRS), operated by VTS San Francisco and described by NAVCEN as completely voluntary; geographic extent not stated
record.evidence_summary: Statutory VTS area (38 nm arc) and the 2025 user manual explicitly cover the San Francisco Offshore TSS; only the outermost ~0.8 nm of the Northern approach extended in 2013 lies outside the arc. The manual notes that a small part of the arc is outside US navigable waters. No MRS; voluntary OVMRS recorded separately.
record.source_date: 33 CFR 161.50 (eCFR 2026-09-01); VTS SF User Manual 1 Apr 2025; COLREG.2/Circ.64 (4 Dec 2012); NAVCEN page accessed 2026-09-29
record.unresolved_issue: Minor: the outer tip of the Northern approach is about 0.8 nm beyond the 38 nm arc; the OVMRS extent is not documented.
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: VTS only confirmed, but coverage is partial (not whole) because the 2013 IMO amendment extended the Northern approach to about 38.8 nm; the lead used the pre-2013 CFR coordinates

sources.date_or_edition: Revised 1 April 2021 (current edition linked from NAVCEN on 2026-09-29)
sources.supports: VTS LA-LB coverage 25 nm seaward of Point Fermin to berth; San Pedro Traffic jointly operated by USCG and Marine Exchange; only portions of the LA-LB TSS inside VTS area; TSS rules include Santa Barbara TSS amendment; manual lists LA-LB in 33 CFR 161 as a VMRS
sources.locator: Introduction p.ii; Appendix A.2-A.4 pp. A-4 to A-6
sources.passage: Portions of the Traffic Separation Scheme in the Northern and Southern approaches to Los Angeles and Long Beach are within the VTS area.

sources.authority: Los Angeles/Long Beach Harbor Safety Committee (published by Marine Exchange of Southern California)
sources.title: LA/LB Harbor Safety Plan, Chapter I Geographical Boundaries
sources.supports: Confirms partial VTS coverage of the LA-LB TSS; describes a 'Northern Approach' (Santa Barbara Channel) separation zone to about 33°48.9'N 118°46.6'W, which conflicts with the IMO COLREG.2/Circ.64 junction point
sources.locator: pp. I-1 to I-3, items A.2 and A.4
sources.passage: portions of the TSS in the western and southern approaches to the LA/LB Harbors lie within the VTS Area of Responsibility.

sources.title: 33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 to s.161.12(c), entry (4) Los Angeles-Long Beach
sources.supports: San Pedro Traffic Ch 14; Vessel Movement Reporting System Area defined as navigable waters within 25 nm of Point Fermin Light. Part 161 contains no separate VTS-area section for LA-LB.
sources.passage: Vessel Movement Reporting System Area: The navigable waters within a 25 nautical mile radius of Point Fermin Light (33°42.30′ N., 118°17.60′ W.).

sources.authority: IMO (compilation hosted by Swedish Transport Agency)
sources.title: COLREG.2/Circ.64, New and amended existing traffic separation schemes, Annexes 6 (Santa Barbara Channel), 7 (Off San Francisco), 8 (Approaches to Los Angeles - Long Beach)
sources.date_or_edition: 4 December 2012 (MSC 91); implemented 1 June 2013; compilation file last modified 2017-05-04; accessed 2026-09-29
sources.supports: Current IMO coordinates: SF northern approach extended to about 38°10'N 123°21'W; Santa Barbara Part I SE end at 33°44.06'N 118°36.34'W joining LA-LB western approach
sources.passage: (A continuation of the Santa Barbara Channel scheme)

sources.authority: Global VTS project (derived from IMO Ships' Routeing 2025 Part I)
sources.title: data/authoritative/IMO_2025_Mandatory_Reporting_Systems.csv
sources.supports: Complete list of IMO-adopted mandatory ship reporting systems (VRS-0001 to VRS-0023); none covers the North American Pacific coast or Mexico (VRS-0021 is the US Atlantic right whale system)
sources.passage: I-I/21,Off the north-eastern and south-eastern coasts of the United States
